Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 1:41: Now, all these aspects mentioned regarding the greatness of our Creator, the Creator of all - that He is great and dominant, and so on - a similar explanation is found in Ra'aya Meheimna, Parashat Pinchas (Zohar 225a), where the explanation is expanded further, in these words: "But regarding the Cause above all, who is called 'the LORD,' it is said of Him, 'to whom will you liken Me, that I should be equal?' says the Holy One (Isaiah 40:25); 'and to whom will you liken God, and what likeness will you compare to Him?' 'I am the LORD, I have not changed' - no sin can reach Him so as to separate the letters Yud from Heh, Vav from Heh, for there is no separation; and of Him it is said, 'no evil shall dwell with You' - He dominates all, and none dominates Him; He grasps all, and none grasps Him; and He is not called 'the LORD,' nor by any [other] Name, except through the spreading of His light upon them, and when He withdraws from them, He has, of Himself, no name at all from them - deep, deep, who can find it? No light is able to gaze upon Him, for even the supernal crown grows dark before Him, whose light is mightier than all the hosts of heaven, upper and lower, and of all the [other] grades it is said, 'He made darkness His hiding place' - and [this applies] to Chochmah and Binah, 'and thick cloud round about Him' - how much more so the other sefirot, how much more so the Chayot [angelic beings], how much more so the [lowest] foundations, which are 'dead bodies.' He surrounds all the worlds, and none surrounds Him, on any side, above, below, or the four directions, save Him alone, and none can go out from His dominion. He fills all the worlds, and none but Him fills them, and there is no god above Him to give Him life - this is [the meaning of] (Nehemiah 9:6), 'and You give life to them all'; and concerning this Daniel said (4:32), 'and all the inhabitants of the earth are accounted as nothing, and He does according to His will with the host of heaven.' He binds and unites each kind with its kind, above and below, and there is no closeness for them through the four elements except through the Holy One, blessed be He, when He is among them" - to the extent relevant here. And when the reader examines this passage carefully, he will understand the first passage of Rashbi, peace be upon him, concerning "great and dominant, foundation," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 1:42: As for what is said (Zohar I 11b), "and to place His will in that place which is called fear" - the intent is that all the aspects mentioned are revealed through it [the Shechinah], for the Name "the LORD" is called great and dominant; but where does His greatness become great? Through it [the Shechinah], as it is written (Psalms 48:2), "great is the LORD and highly praised, in the city of our God, His holy mountain" - as is explained in Parashat Vayikra (Zohar 5a) on this verse, in these words: "It is heard that a king without a queen is not [truly] a king, and is not great, and is not praised."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 1:43: This matter is further explained in the Tikkunim in many places, in particular one passage (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash 103a) found among us in manuscript, in these words: "'and the wise shall shine' (Daniel 12:3) - who are the wise? Those who have the understanding to know the Master of the world, who is above all supernal beings, through the Shechinah, of which it is said (Psalms 118:20), 'this is the gate of the LORD, the righteous shall enter through it' - Sha'ar [gate], when its letters are reversed, [spells] Esser [ten], comprising the ten sefirot," and so on. And he said at the end of the discourse: "and because He is within, the faith of Israel was placed in her, for she is bound to all the inner and outer [levels], for she comprises the upper and lower beings without end or limit; and therefore she is called the faith of Israel, and through her the upper and lower beings, and the Cause above all supernal beings, become known; and whoever unifies Him through her is as one who unifies Him and crowns Him over all the upper and lower beings" - to this point are his words. And so too in Parashat Terumah (Zohar 158b), see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 1:44: Further, in Ra'aya Meheimna, Parashat Pinchas (230a), it is explained even more clearly, in these words: "This is the holy kingship [Malchut], which is the image of all, through which the Holy One, blessed be He, looked and created the world and all the creatures He created in the world, and comprises within her the upper and lower beings without any separation at all, and comprises within her the ten sefirot and all their names and appellations and forms of being; and the Cause above all, who is Master of all and beside whom there is no god, is found among the upper and lower beings to no lesser degree than her, for she is the bond of them all, the completeness of them all, so that His kingship rules over all through her - for the Cause above all is not found among the upper and lower beings to a lesser degree than her, even in a single one of them; she is called the faith of Israel" - to the extent relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 1:45: Further, in the Tikkunim, in manuscript (Tikkunim Chadashim 10a): "and from the side of the three Patriarchs, who are called El, Elohim, and the LORD, who are 'the great, mighty, and awesome God' - they are called Gedulah [Greatness], Gevurah [Might], and Tiferet [Beauty], and through these three names she [the Shechinah] testifies to His being, His Godhood, and His power over all the worlds. And from the side of the supernal Mother she is called 'Mother,' 'repentance,' 'the LORD,' which indicates an appellation - for the [Name] Havayah of the Master of the world is the master of all appellations and all forms of being, which are appellations for Him, while He Himself is not an appellation. And she is called Mah [what] from the side of Chochmah, of which it is said (Deuteronomy 11:11 [12]), 'what [mah] does the LORD your God ask of you, but to fear...' - for if there is no wisdom there is no fear, and if there is no fear there is no wisdom; and through this Mah she testifies concerning the Cause of all supernal beings, that they do not know what He is" - to the extent relevant here. Behold, the revelation of His Godhood and power to the King [malka, i.e., to created beings] comes about through her; if so, it is fitting that "great and dominant, foundation and root," through which everything is revealed, should be attributed to her.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 1:46: Likewise in the Writings we find this attribute of greatness and dominion attributed to her as well: "great is our Lord, and mighty in power," and so on (Psalms 147:5). And so too what is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Bereshit (19a), on the verse (Lamentations 3:23), "they are new every morning, great is Your faithfulness" - see there. And likewise (Psalms 145:13), "Your kingdom is a kingdom for all ages, and Your dominion is throughout all generations" - and the aspect of being the foundation and root of all worlds is also stated in "Your kingdom is a kingdom for all ages"; its meaning may be understood through the secret that "the end of the deed is first in thought" - see the Tikkunim (11a) concerning (Proverbs 8:22), "the LORD made me as the beginning of His way...
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 1:47: There is no need to elaborate further on this aspect, for since "the LORD" is the foundation and root of all worlds, as I have explained above, and the revelation of His action through them is as I have explained above - that she is called Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet, who testifies to His Godhood, and so on, and "everything before Him is as nothing" - this aspect too is found within her.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 1:48: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained this in connection with the verse (I Kings 5:10), "and Solomon's wisdom increased," and so on. He said there, in Parashat Vayechi (Zohar 223a): "The moon - a thousand great mountains stood before her, and they were all as a single breath before her; a thousand abundant rivers were hers, and in a single swallow she swallowed them" - to the extent relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 1:49: Likewise in Parashat Pinchas (Zohar 240b), in these words: "Rather, it is a secret, for there is a beast that crouches over a thousand mountains, and it devours a thousand mountains every day, and they are all called 'beasts'; and concerning this we have learned that there is a beast that devours beasts. And from what were they [the mountains] made? Of fire, and that beast licks them all up in a single lick, as it is written (Deuteronomy 4:24), 'for the LORD your God is a consuming fire, a jealous God.' And all the water of the Jordan, though it fills for six years, she makes into a single swallow, as it is written (Job 40:23), 'he is confident that he can draw up the Jordan into his mouth'" - to the extent relevant here. And upon the secret of this beast depends the arousal of the lower beings, whose essence is in the secret of Ben [son] from Binyamin, and this is the secret of "let no oil be lacking on your head," as I explained in the Gate of Love, at the beginning of chapter 5.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 1:50: It may be said that these four aspects mentioned - "great, and dominant, foundation," and so on, and "everything before Him is as nothing" - correspond to the four letters of the Tetragrammaton, and are revealed through the Name Adnut [Adonai]; and there is no room to elaborate further here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 1:51: All the aspects of fear that I have explained as flowing from His being "great and dominant, foundation," and so on, are all present in the Shechinah in relation to the lower beings. For from her side come the souls of Israel, and likewise the vitality of all the lower beings; and when a person dies, the soul returns to her, as is explained in Parashat Vayechi (Zohar 217b), in these words: "Rabbi Yehuda said: at the time when a person's feet become bound and his days draw near, that day is called 'the day of the LORD,' to return his spirit to Him. We have learned in that teaching that this holy crown [i.e., the Shechinah] is appointed over his spirit; and who is she? As it is written (Psalms 90:10), 'the days of our years among them are seventy years' - and she is the seventh crown of all" - to the extent relevant here. Therefore one must fear her, for it is in her power to remove the soul in an instant; and this is [the meaning of] (Daniel 5:23), "and the God in whose hand is your breath, and all your ways, are His," and so on; and likewise (Job 12:10), "in whose hand is the soul of every living thing, and the breath of all mankind" - for the Shechinah is called "hand," and the explanation of this verse will be given in the next chapter, with God's help.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 1:52: Also the aspect I explained, that it is not fitting to sin and be ungrateful for all the good that the Holy One, blessed be He, has done for one - this aspect too is from her side, for she is the mother who raises us; one must fear her judgment and love her for her mercy, and this is the fear that leads to love.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 1:53: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained this aspect in the Pekudin printed in Parashat Va'etchanan (Zohar 263b), in these words: "The commandment to fear, in a general way and in a particular way, has already been established, for a person must fear before the Holy One, blessed be He, always; and through fear he will guard his ways. And 'fear' is [also] a place that is called 'fear,' as it says (Deuteronomy 28:58), 'to fear this glorious and awesome Name, the LORD your God' - for there [in that place] the fear of the Holy One, blessed be He, dwells, and that itself is fear, to fear it. And this is the secret of what is written, 'and you shall fear My sanctuary' - in this fear dwells the fiery lash to punish the wicked who do not keep the commandments of the Torah. And therefore, in a general way one must fear; and afterward, in a particular way, when a person knows what the fear of the LORD is - this is the fear of love, which is the foundation and root for loving the Holy One, blessed be He. After this fear, one keeps all the commandments of the Torah, so that a person becomes a faithful servant to the Holy One, blessed be He, as fitting fear requires" - to the extent relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 1:54: My teacher, peace be upon him, wrote concerning the statement "when he knows what the fear of the LORD is," and so on, that the intent is that one should fear lest, through his sins, he cause the Shechinah to be separated from the Name "the LORD," which is Tiferet; and he should say in his heart: how could I, through my sins, cause the love between the beloved and the friend to be separated, and thereby become a talebearer who separates the closest of friends? We find, then, that this aspect of fear is a fear that leads to love, for it is not enough that one should not sin, but one should also strive to perform a commandment in order to unify and draw near the love. However, in the previous fear, which is fear of punishment - one who fears performs a commandment because he fears excision [karet], such as not to neglect the commandment of circumcision, for which one is liable to karet, or not to eat forbidden fat, for which one is liable to karet - certainly, one who acts only out of fear of punishment will not exert himself in fulfilling the commandments [beyond avoiding punishment]. So concludes his words, in summary.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 1:55: Now, for the reason we have stated above, that in the Shechinah is revealed His being "great and dominant," and so on, Rashbi, peace be upon him, said there, in Parashat Bereshit (Zohar 11b), in these words: "And therefore the place that is called 'the fear of the LORD' is called 'beginning' [reishit]; and therefore this commandment is included here, and this is the foundation and basis for all the other commandments of the Torah. Whoever guards fear guards everything; whoever does not guard fear does not guard the commandments of the Torah, for this is the gate to everything. And therefore it is written 'bereishit' [in the beginning], which is fear, 'God created the heavens and the earth'" - to the extent relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:1: Among the things that arouse the inner fear discussed in the previous chapter, the first is for a person to contemplate, with his intellect, the works of the Holy One, blessed be He; for in their vastness they instill fear, as King David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 66:3), "say to God, how awesome are Your works." And likewise Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, in the passage "and now, Israel, what does the LORD your God ask of you, but to fear" (Deuteronomy 10:12), said (ibid. 10:14), "behold, to the LORD your God belong the heavens, and the heaven of heavens, the earth and all that is in it" - it appears that this is among the things that arouse fear.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:2: This matter is explained in the words of our Sages, of blessed memory, and in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, and we must cite their words, of blessed memory, in order to arouse the heart to fear. In tractate Chagigah (13a), in these words: "From the earth to the firmament is a journey of five hundred years, and the thickness of the firmament is a journey of five hundred years, and so between each firmament [there is the same distance]; above them are the Holy Chayot [angelic beings] - the legs of the Chayot correspond to all of them [in size], the ankles of the Chayot correspond to all of them, the shins of the Chayot correspond to all of them, the knees of the Chayot correspond to all of them, the thighs of the Chayot correspond to all of them, the bodies of the Chayot correspond to all of them, the necks of the Chayot correspond to all of them, the heads of the Chayot correspond to all of them, the horns of the Chayot correspond to all of them; above them is the Throne of Glory - the legs of the Throne of Glory correspond to all of them, the Throne of Glory [itself] corresponds to all of them; the King, the living and eternal God, high and exalted, dwells above them" - to the extent relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:3: And in Parashat Beshalach (56b), on the verse (Exodus 15:4), "Pharaoh's chariots and his army He cast into the sea," this matter is explained further, in these words: "Rabbi Yitzchak opened [with the verse] (Jeremiah 10:12-13), 'at the sound of His giving, a multitude of waters in the heavens...' We have learned that the Holy One, blessed be He, made seven firmaments, and in each and every firmament stars are set and run their course, and above them all is Aravot; and each and every firmament takes two hundred years to traverse, and its height is five hundred years, and between one firmament and the next is five hundred years; and this Aravot is, in its length, a journey of one thousand five hundred years, and in its breadth one thousand five hundred years, and from its radiance all those firmaments shine. And we have learned that above Aravot is the span [width] of the Holy Chayot, whose height is like all of them [combined] above them, and the ankles of the Chayot are like all of them," and so on - so far what is explained in the Talmud - to the extent relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:4: Further (58a), in the same passage: we have learned that his name is Hadarniel, and he is greater than the other angels by twelve thousand ten-thousands of parasangs, and his voice travels through two hundred thousand firmaments that revolve in white fire - to the extent relevant here. This is the second angel that Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, encountered when he ascended to receive the Torah, and Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, was afraid of this angel, until he mentioned the Name of seventy-two [letters]; and once this angel heard the letters of the Name, he trembled and drew near to him. And afterward the passage says: and he went with him until they reached the mighty fire of an angel named Sandalfon; and we have learned that Sandalfon is greater than his fellows by a journey of five hundred years, and he stands behind the curtain of his Master and binds crowns from the pleas of Israel's prayers; and at the time when this crown reaches the head of the Holy King, He accepts the prayer of Israel, and all the hosts and multitudes tremble and say, "blessed is the glory of the LORD from the place of His Shechinah's dwelling." Hadarniel said to Moses: I cannot go with you further, lest the mighty fire of Sandalfon burn me. At that moment Moses trembled, until the Holy One, blessed be He, took hold of Moses and set him before Him, and so on - to the extent relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:5: Now, from the greatness of the servants the greatness of the Master becomes known; for if His angels are of such great stature, how much more so the greatness of His attributes in Atzilut, and how much more so His own greatness, blessed be He, which has no end or limit - especially for those who see the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in his explanation in Idra Naso (127b-145a) concerning the multitude of the worlds within Atzilut - "these have seen the works of the LORD and His wonders." And it is said in the Tikkunim (135b): "the supernal crown, even though it is a primordial light, a pure light, a polished light, is dark before the Cause of causes" - to the extent relevant here. And it is with respect to this aspect of the great illumination, which has no limit, that the Infinite is called "great," as I explained above (chapter 1), by the way.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:6: Now, when a person contemplates His works, blessed be He, he will fear and be humbled by His greatness, and feel shame before Him, and not transgress His command. And so said Jonah the prophet (Jonah 1:9), "and I fear the LORD, the God of heaven, who made the sea and the dry land." It appears that fear comes from His works, which display His greatness. And so said King David, peace be upon him (Psalms 8:4-5), "when I see Your heavens, the work of Your fingers, the moon and the stars which You have established - what is man, that You are mindful of him?" And so said Moses our teacher, peace be upon him (Exodus 16:7), "and what are we?" - for we do not enter the category of a [significant] creature compared to His greatness, blessed be He, as it is written (Daniel 4:32), "and all the inhabitants of the earth are accounted as nothing."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:7: There is a second aspect that arouses fear, close to the one mentioned, and it is for a person to reflect, with his understanding, upon the signs and wonders that occur anew in the world. Thus Israel, when they saw the great miracle done for them at the sea, fear is stated of them, as it is said (Exodus 14:31), "and Israel saw the great hand that the LORD had wrought against Egypt, and the people feared the LORD," and so on. And so said the Psalmist (Psalms 65:7-9), "who forms the mountains by His strength, girded with might, who stills the roaring of the seas, the roaring of their waves, and the tumult of the peoples; and those who dwell at the ends of the earth are afraid at Your signs; You make the outgoings of the morning and evening to rejoice," and so on - and the other wonders and signs of the LORD, blessed be He, mentioned in this psalm.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:8: There is a third aspect that arouses fear, likewise close to the one just mentioned, and it is for a person to reflect upon the abundant good that the Creator bestows upon him beyond his due. This is what the prophet said (Malachi 1:6), "and if I am a father, where is My honor?... where is My fear?" For it is the way of a father to do good and show mercy to his son, and if the son sins, the father chastises him, as it is said (Proverbs 1:8), "hear, my son, your father's instruction." And this is what the prophet Jeremiah, peace be upon him, said (Jeremiah 5:24), "neither say they in their heart, let us now fear the LORD our God, who gives rain, the early and the late rain in its season, who keeps for us the appointed weeks of the harvest... your iniquities have turned away these things, and your sins have withheld good from you." Here it explicitly states fear arising from goodness, as it says, "let us now fear... who gives rain," and so on; "your iniquities have turned away these things" - this refers to sufferings. And the fear is not on account of the sufferings, but because it is the father's way to do good and show mercy, and one must fear lest he himself be the cause that makes his father act cruelly toward him and withhold good from him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:9: Regarding this aspect of fear, one may explain what is explained in the Tikkunim (129a) and in the Zohar, Parashat Naso (122b): the letter Yud [of Yirah, "fear"] is upon a person's head, and from it fear enters a person's heart, to fear the Holy One, blessed be He, and to guard himself from transgressing the commandments - to the extent relevant here. And so it is also explained in the Midrash on Ruth, from the Zohar (82b).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:10: Regarding this aspect of fear, one may explain the verse (Deuteronomy 28:58), "to fear this glorious [nichbad] and awesome Name," and so on - for there is an aspect in which He is called "glorious" [nichbad] in respect of the goodness that flows from Him, as will be explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:11: "Kavod" [glory/honor] is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Pekudei (221b), to mean "illumination," in connection with the verse (Isaiah 11:10), "the root of Jesse, who stands as a banner for the peoples, to him shall the nations seek, and his resting place shall be glory [kavod]" - in these words: "'and his resting place shall be glory' - his resting place is the Temple; 'glory' - for at that time it will be called 'glory,' as it is written (ibid. 30:26), 'and the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun, and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold' - and the resting place of that root of Jesse is called the glory of the LORD, which cannot be numbered and will not be reckoned in the world" - to the extent relevant here. Here it is explicitly stated that when it is called "glory," it means that it rises to the level of great illumination, so that the light of the moon becomes as the light of the sun, and then it is no longer bound by measure and number, as it was when it was below, as it is written (Song of Songs 7:5), "your eyes are like pools in Cheshbon [also: 'reckoning'], by the gate of Bat Rabbim," as is explained in Parashat Pinchas (Zohar 220b); and so it is also explained in Parashat Bereshit (8a), on the verse (Psalms 19:2), "the heavens declare the glory of God" - that "glory" means illumination and importance, see there. And we find in the verses that "glory" refers to light: in Isaiah (60:1), "and the glory of the LORD has risen upon you"; in Ezekiel (43:2), "and the earth shone with His glory"; and in the Torah (Exodus 40:34), "and the glory of the LORD filled the Tabernacle"; and likewise (Leviticus 9:6), "and the glory of the LORD shall appear to you" - and many more like these.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:12: One may also relate "kavod" to meaning "light" because the Targum renders "kavod" as "yekar" [preciousness/brightness], and it is written (Zechariah 14:6), "and it shall come to pass in that day, there shall be no light, [only] preciousness and thick darkness [yekarot ve-kipa'on]" - and the intent is bright light, for "yekar" is importance, and light has no importance except through its brightness.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:13: And so, when it is said (Isaiah 11:10), "and his resting place shall be glory" - the "glory" is that it rises in level and importance; and what is the importance above, in Atzilut? The brightness of its light, that the light of the moon should be as the light of the sun.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:14: And so, in Ra'aya Meheimna, in Parashat Pinchas (Zohar 225b), it is explained that what Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, said (Exodus 33:18), "show me, please, Your glory," referred to the supernal crown [Keter], in these words: "and therefore the measure of a sukkah [booth] is no less than ten [handbreadths], for it is Malchut, tenth of all the grades, and no higher than twenty, for that is the supernal crown, upon which no eye can rule. Concerning the supernal glory Moses said, 'show me, please, Your glory,' and the Holy One, blessed be He, answered him, 'you cannot see My face,' for there is no 'kavod' [glory] without a 'kaf'" - to the extent relevant here. If so, we find that it is from the aspect of the illumination of the bright light that comes from above that it is called "kavod," as it says, "there is no glory without a kaf." And this refines the language of the passage above, which said, "it is called the glory of the LORD, which will not be numbered," and so on; and similar to this (Exodus 33:22), "and it shall come to pass, while My glory passes by, that I will put you in a cleft [of the rock]," and so on; and likewise in Job (19:9), "he has stripped my glory from me," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:15: We find, then, that when it says "the glorious Name" [ha-shem ha-nichbad], the intent is that He is the source of illumination for all creatures, for they all receive light and flow from "the LORD," as I explained in the previous chapter; and this is what I explained, that "nichbad" [glorious] indicates the good that flows from Him, blessed be He.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:16: With this one may understand what is said in the Zohar, Parashat Vayelech (241b): "he who directs his intention to unify the Name - of him it is said, 'for those who honor Me, I will honor' [Bechavod - I Samuel 2:30]." And the reason is that through his good intention he draws forth additional illumination above, as is explained there regarding the manner of unification; and therefore from there illumination is drawn to his soul in the World to Come, and this is his "kavod" [glory/honor].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:17: "And awesome" [ve-hanora] - the explanation is as was explained above, in the passage we cited from Parashat Beshalach, that even among the angels, one whose angel is greater than his fellow, the others fear to approach him; and likewise (Exodus 34:30), "and they were afraid to approach him," said of Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, because of the shining of his face. And it is said in the Zohar, Parashat Beshalach (58a), that when Israel sinned with the [golden] calf, the Holy One, blessed be He, took from Moses a thousand portions of that radiance, and from the radiance that remained in him, Moses' face shone; and if, with what remained in him, they could not gaze upon his face, how much more so with what was taken from him! - to the extent relevant here. And similarly it is said regarding "and awesome" - for from His being "glorious" [nichbad], in the manner we explained, it follows that He is "awesome" [nora], for all the hosts above fear to approach Him because of His light, which has no limit, lest their existence be nullified - in the manner explained in the book Brit Menuchah concerning the "graves of desire" [Kivrot ha-Ta'avah], for there they buried the people who desired [too much], for any angel who desires and craves to rise above his own level, his existence is nullified; and this is the matter of "burial" arising from desire, which is craving.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:18: In this manner one may also explain (Ecclesiastes 12:13), "fear God and keep His commandments, for this is the whole of man" - the matter being that there is an "Adam" [man] of Atzilut, an "Adam" of Beriah, an "Adam" of Yetzirah, and an "Adam" of Asiyah, as is explained in the Tikkunim (41b); and all the aspects of "Adam" mentioned have their own fear, that the "Adam" of Beriah should not enter to look and gaze upon what is above his own level, which is in Atzilut, and likewise for the others. And not only this, but even within Atzilut itself, it is explained in the Tikkunim (119a) that there is no sefirah that is not called "Adam," and all the aspects of "Adam" within Atzilut have this fear mentioned - so that even the Keter itself, in a certain small measure, has this fear, since it too is emanated and is dark before the Cause of causes; it fears the Cause above all causes. And this is [the meaning of] "for this is the whole of Adam" - meaning, all the aspects of "Adam" mentioned have this fear.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:19: In this manner my teacher, peace be upon him, explained, in the book Tefillah LeMoshe, these verses (Psalms 48:5-7): "for behold, the kings assembled, they passed by together; they saw, so they were astounded, they were dismayed, they hastened away; trembling took hold of them there, pain as of a woman in labor" - for all this occurs at the time of the ascent of the [heavenly] chambers, rising upward, and when they arrive there, "they saw, so they were astounded," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:20: There is yet another way to explain "the glorious and awesome," close to the way already stated: we find that the soul is called "glory" [kavod], as it is said (Psalms 30:13), "so that my glory may sing praise to You and not be silent"; and likewise (ibid. 16:9), "therefore my heart is glad, and my glory rejoices." For a person's glory, that which gives him light, is the soul; if so, "the Glorious One" means that He is the source of all souls - and not only the souls of the lower beings, but He is the source of illumination that gives light to all the upper worlds, and He is, as it were, the soul within them; and just as the soul gives light to the body, so He, blessed be He, is the source of the soul for them all.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:21: "And the awesome" [ve-hanora], according to this, is because, since "in His hand is the soul of every living thing, and the breath of all mankind" (Job 12:10), one must fear Him, for it is in His hand to remove the soul in an instant, so that "all flesh would perish together," as it is written (Daniel 5:23), "and the God in whose hand is your breath, and all your ways, are His, you have not glorified." And correspondingly, all the hosts above fear Him as well, since their flow and vitality depend on Him; and this is [the meaning of] "in whose hand is the soul of every living thing" - referring to the hosts above, who live and endure forever, and their vitality depends upon Him, blessed be He; and "every living thing" [kol chai] serves to include, up to the very highest, the entire reality of the emanated beings. "And the breath of all flesh of man" refers to the physical, lower beings in the lower [world of] Asiyah, and therefore the term "flesh" is used for them, because death and destruction rule over them; whereas regarding the upper beings, in whom there is no death, it says "every living thing," for they all live from His vitality, blessed be He, as it is said (Nehemiah 9:6), "and You give life to them all."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:22: Further, we find that Scripture uses the word "kavod" in the sense of praise and glorification, as in (Psalms 29:9), "and in His Temple, all say 'Glory'" - meaning the praise and glorification uttered to the LORD, blessed be He. And in Ra'aya Meheimna, Parashat Kedoshim (81b), it is explained that "kavod" has the numerical value of thirty-two, referring to the thirty-two paths of wisdom. And it is known, as stated in Sefer Yetzirah, that with the thirty-two paths of wisdom, which are the thirty-two "Elohim" [occurrences of the divine name in the account] of the work of creation, He engraved Yah, the LORD of Hosts, His world. The meaning is that through these thirty-two paths came the creation of all the worlds, which is the matter of the entire work of creation; and the thirty-two paths are associated with the word "kavod" because the glory of the Holy One, blessed be He, is revealed to us through His works and the great creatures He created, as I explained at the beginning of this chapter, and through this we glorify and praise Him, as it is said (Isaiah 43:7), "all who are called by My Name, and whom I created for My glory" - meaning that he should glorify Me and praise Me; for this I created him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:23: Further, "the Glorious One" may mean, as explained in Ra'aya Meheimna which we cited above at the end of chapter 1, on (Isaiah 6:3), "the whole earth is full of His glory" - this refers to the glory of His Godhood, blessed be He, which is revealed to us through the spreading forth of the worlds from cause to effect, as it says: "for if His light did not spread over all creatures, how would they recognize Him, and how would 'the whole earth is full of His glory' be fulfilled?" And the glory of His Godhood is revealed through the kaf of "keter" [crown], for there is no "kavod" without a "kaf," as I explained above; and afterward the light is clothed through the thirty-two paths of wisdom, which are the ten utterances and the twenty-two letters, as is explained in the Tikkunim (78b); and through the thirty-two paths, by which the entire work of creation was accomplished, "the whole earth is full of His glory" is fulfilled. And from this aspect "the LORD" is called "glorious," for through Him the creation of everything came about through the thirty-two paths, and He comprises them all.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:24: He is also "glorious" in the sense that He is bound forever and comprises the glory of the supernal Godhood through the crown, which is the "kaf," as is explained in the Tikkunim, which we cited above in chapter 1: the Name is not called by the unity of the four letters alone, but by the unity of the Cause of causes who unifies them; and through this glory it spreads downward to the lower beings, in the secret of "the whole earth is full of His glory," as I explained in chapter 1. And with this explanation, all the interpretations we have given regarding "the Glorious One" converge upon a single path.
